items.summary: The Thunder have gone 5-5 since they lost Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren to long-term injuries. Williams and Wallace might be out for the season, while Holmgren likely won’t return until at least January. While Oklahoma City’s ceiling and floor have both dropped considerably in the wake of the devastating injuries, the team still has some adjustments it could try to make the most of the situation it was dealt, according to Rylan Stiles of SI.com, who writes that running opposing shooters off the three-point line and funneling them into the paint would be one option. Stiles acknowledges it would be difficult for the Thunder to change their defense mid-season, but views the available personnel as incapable of playing their preferred style. items.title: Jazz Discussed Trade Involving Isaiah Collier, Tre Jones
items.summary: The Jazz have had recent trade talks involving point guard Isaiah Collier, league sources tell Grant Afseth of FastBreakJournal.com. According to Afseth, Tre Jones was among the players the Jazz targeted in those discussions, but the Bulls weren’t interested in Utah’s offer. Afseth hears multiple teams have expressed interest in Jones and says the Bulls would want “meaningful compensation” to consider moving the veteran point guard, whose market is “strong.” Chicago also likes Jones and values him as a top-tier backup, sources tell Afseth. Jones is earning $8MM this season and his contract features an $8MM team option for 2027/28. Utah declined its fourth-year option on Collier earlier this month. items.title: Wolves Or Grizzlies Likely To Switch To East If NBA Adds Two Teams
items.summary: If the NBA adds expansion franchises in Las Vegas and Seattle, then one current Western Conference team would have to move to the East as part of realignment. The Grizzlies or Timberwolves are considered the most likely teams to switch conferences in that scenario, eight league sources told Joe Vardon, Mike Vorkunov and Sam Amick of The Athletic (free link). “Both of those teams are vying to go east,” one source told The Athletic. As the authors explain, proximity is one reason why those two teams are vying to switch conferences. But the main motivating factor is they think it’ll give them an easier pathway to reach the NBA Finals. The Pelicans are also a candidate to move to the East, but that outcome is viewed as less likely in part because New Orleans is closer to the three Texas teams and Oklahoma City. “I wouldn’t say New Orleans is off the table, because nothing’s been decided…

items.summary: The Heat won their sixth straight game on Wednesday against Milwaukee behind big games from star big men Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. items.title: Raptors’ RJ Barrett (Hamstring) Out At Least Two Weeks
items.summary: Forward RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain, the Raptors announced today (Twitter link via Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca). According to the team, another update on Barrett will come in two weeks, which means he’ll miss at least five more games after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to Washington because of the injury. Barrett will likely be reevaluated ahead of the December 3 contest in San Antonio. Barrett’s hamstring injury occurred in Tuesday’s loss to New York. He underwent imaging, which confirmed the strain. In 14 appearances this season, the Toronto native has averaged 20.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and 4.3 assists in 34.1 minutes per game, with a shooting slash line of .473/.284/.608.
